messages:
marta: FYI I found a reproducible "ghost" duplication during long-prefill bring-up for nova-128k-int4. Looks like KV reads are returning stale vectors duplicated across adjacent slots after a rebalance event. Repro details below.

josh: Oof. Which runtime + quant?

marta: runtime: main@d7c9a (recent rebalance/reshard optimizations). quant: int4-packed-v3. Cmd: 
```bash
python tools/long_onboard.py \\
  --model nova-128k-int4 \\
  --context 128500 \\
  --prefill 128200 \\
  --quant int4-packed-v3 \\
  --kv-rebalance auto \\
  --rotary-phase-mode dynamic \\
  --save /tmp/nova-repro.tar.gz
```

marta: Short log fragment: 
```
[2026-01-12T08:22:11Z] prefill=128214
[2026-01-12T08:22:11Z] kv_read: token=128064 -> slot=1024 owner=worker-3
[2026-01-12T08:22:11Z] kv_read: token=128065 -> slot=1025 owner=worker-3
[2026-01-12T08:22:12Z] rebalance: moving slot=1025 -> worker-5
[2026-01-12T08:22:12Z] kv_read: token=128066 -> slot=1026 owner=worker-3
[2026-01-12T08:22:12Z] kv_read: token=128067 -> slot=1027 owner=worker-3
[2026-01-12T08:22:12Z] kv_read: token=128068 -> slot=1028 owner=worker-5  <-- expected new owner
[2026-01-12T08:22:13Z] generation: token=128210 detected duplicated fingerprint: slot=1028==slot=1026
```

rachel: duplicated fingerprint between non-adjacent slots? that's odd. Any indication of slot aliasing or cache-line reuse?

marta: ran `--dump-kv-fingerprints 1024:1032` and got: 
```
1024: 0x9ab1c3
1025: 0x9ab1c8
1026: 0x9ab1d5
1027: 0x9ab1d5  <-- duplicate with 1026
1028: 0x9ab1e1
```

josh: 1026 & 1027 identical before rebalance? but your log showed 1027 owned by worker-3; then rebalance moved 1025. Could be a race where slot remapping occurred while an async write was in-flight and completion acknowledged to wrong slot. Also rotary-phase-mode dynamic was recently changed to apply phase deltas during rebalance; maybe phase update code reuses temporary buffers.

marta: good point. I reran with `--kv-rebalance off --rotary-phase-mode static` and the duplication disappears. So two potential interacting factors.

bench-bot: quick triangulation: 
- baseline fp16: no dup 
- int4-packed-v3 with rebalance=auto + rotary=dynamic: dup 5/5 
- int4-packed-v3 with rebalance=off: no dup 5/5

rachel: please try `--kv-atomic-commit` and `--rotary-phase-droop` flags. Atomic commit will force atomic remap and phase-droop applies phase patching in-place more conservatively. If that fixes, it's likely a visibility/race bug.

marta: running that now. Also attaching small trace to s3://repro/nova/3287654321/trace.tar.gz.

marta: result: `--kv-atomic-commit --rotary-phase-droop` -> passes 4/4. With atomic commit only -> 2/4 dup. With phase-droop only -> 1/4 dup. So both reduce the issue but atomic commit more effective.

josh: that suggests two contributing issues: (1) a non-atomic remap that allows reads to observe a slot in an interim state (zeroed header + partial payload), and (2) rotary-phase dynamic patching that reuses scratch memory which can transiently overwrite in-flight buffers. Combined they produce duplicated fingerprint reads because the writer can write to temp buffer that gets mapped into a different slot address before the write completes.

rachel: runtime: can you add a quick guard to ensure remap() sets a tombstone flag and waits for outstanding read/write epoch to finish before switching ownership? Also audit `phase_apply()` for any non-threadsafe temp buffers.

eng-runtime: acknowledged. I'll PR a conservative remap (tombstone+fence) behind flag KV_REMAP_SAFE for quick canary. Also adding an ASAN/Tsan stress job to long_onboard CI.

marta: created INF-4022 + uploaded minimal repro harness under tests/longctx/nova_rebalance_dup_test.py. I'll open PR linking the S3 trace and bench outputs.

josh: please add a regression microtest that runs the packed int4 codepath with an injected rebalance at a known prefill index so CI can deterministically exercise.

marta: will do. Thanks all. I'll keep this thread updated when runtime PR lands. :white_check_mark:
